clue.text: One searching after man on board gets the bird

indicators.note: after places the searcher behind the chess piece in the answer

parts.note: a king is one of the chessmen on a chessboard
a fisher is one who fishes, i.e. searches or casts about for something

explanation.surface: A chess player looking for something ends up being jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' suggests being booed off; here 'gets' just links and 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured river bird famous for diving after fish.

clue.text: Continue to protect a bird

parts.note: to keep can mean to guard or protect
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to carry on protecting a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning persevere, carry on without stopping.

clue.text: Drink in sort of trance

indicators.note: sort of signals a version of the word, its letters put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone drinks while in a kind of trance.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink of the gods in classical myth, now any delicious beverage or fruit juice.

clue.text: Thief's developed obsession

indicators.note: developed suggests something reworked, so the letters form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A burglar has developed an obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: An irrational fixation or compulsive preoccupation with something.

clue.text: One in a suit or vest being worn

parts.note: a singlet is a sleeveless vest (in British usage, an undershirt)
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: Someone wears either a suit or a vest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing, but it is a suit of playing cards in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games, a lone card held in a particular suit is so called.

clue.text: International organisation visibly embarrassed and angry

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
cross means angry

explanation.surface: An international body is publicly shamed and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The worldwide humanitarian movement providing medical and emergency relief.

clue.text: Face some balls, having put ball in vessel?

indicators.note: having put tells us one piece is being placed into another
in shows the round letter goes inside the cricket word

parts.note: in cricket, to bat is to face the bowler's deliveries
a ball is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricketer faces some deliveries after putting a ball into a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: a vessel in the sense of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel in the nautical sense is a ship or smaller craft on the water.

clue.text: Ernie, possibly a servant

definitions.meaning: ERNIE is the machine that picks winning Premium Bonds numbers in Britain, so jokingly the man for those bonds
a serf or slave bound to serve a master

explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a UK government savings scheme whose prizes are drawn by ERNIE, Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a man in bondage, a serf obliged to work for his lord.

clue.text: Barely sufficient these days to regard as similar

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the present era of dates
to equate things is to treat them as equivalent

explanation.surface: Something only just good enough is nowadays treated as the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: enough to meet a need, though no more than that.

clue.text: Thrilling going to include Charlie

indicators.note: to include means the leaving word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: going out or leaving is exiting
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something thrilling is about to happen because Charlie is coming along.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that stirs excitement and enthusiasm in a person.

clue.text: Risk spoiling garden

indicators.note: spoiling suggests the letters of the plot of land are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: There is a risk of ruining the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a risk or hazard is a peril to be avoided.

clue.text: American blocks beer getting water instead

parts.note: dams are barriers that block a river
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: An American cuts off someone's beer supply, so they have to drink water instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is an old jocular name for plain water, the only drink the first man had.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous idiom for plain drinking water, from the only drink available in Eden.

clue.text: Save engineers given second signal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cue is a signal to act, as for an actor

explanation.surface: Engineers are given a second signal to save something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to save someone is to deliver them from danger.

clue.text: Lady taking only half of mosaic pieces

indicators.note: only half of tells us to keep just the front four of the eight-letter word for the tiles

parts.note: tesserae are the small tiles that make up a mosaic

explanation.surface: A woman takes only half of the tiles for her mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, as in Hardy's heroine of the d'Urbervilles.

clue.text: Instrument reportedly fires round ring

indicators.note: reportedly means the dismissing word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to fire an employee is to sack them, so fires means sacks
round is shaped like the letter O
to ring someone is to phone them

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is said to set off rounds of gunfire in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass-bodied single-reed woodwind used widely in jazz.

clue.text: Lot more quivering with this musical effect

indicators.note: quivering suggests unsteady movement, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A lot more quivering produces this musical effect.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'quivering' also describes the answer itself, a wavering note.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a rapid wavering or repetition of a note produced by a singer or instrument.

clue.text: Heard 'Lady in Red' and felt great joy?

indicators.note: in places the name inside the colour word

parts.note: taken as the word red

indicators.note: heard means the woman's name is taken by sound, spelt differently

parts.note: Joyce is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Hearing the song 'Lady in Red' made someone very happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady in Red' is a Chris de Burgh hit, but here it is pure instruction. 'Heard' means the woman's name is taken by its sound and spelt differently; 'in' puts it inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great gladness, a past tense here.

clue.text: Large number care about carnage

parts.note: a mass is a large number or quantity

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a different order

explanation.surface: A great many people care about carnage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the indiscriminate slaughter of many people.

clue.text: Very much likes to put away chair

parts.note: to love is to like very much
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Someone is very keen to store a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sofa or double armchair for two people sitting together.

clue.text: Like junior perhaps going to pieces

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similarly to
a junior works under someone more senior

explanation.surface: A junior, perhaps, is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means apart, into separate parts, as when something is torn in two.

clue.text: Fetch dog right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the dog

parts.note: a retriever is a gun dog breed

explanation.surface: A dog is told to fetch and run off right away.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to go and bring something back.

clue.text: Stone ring next to New York Times

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like O
the multiplication sign for times looks like X

explanation.surface: A stone ring sits beside a copy of the New York Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York Times' reads as the newspaper, but it splits into NY and Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Governor fighting over place of thieves

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the fighting word above the hideout

parts.note: war is fighting
a den of thieves is a proverbial hideout

explanation.surface: A governor wages a fight over a thieves' den.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden is an official in charge, as the governor of a prison or institution.

clue.text: English itch badly to accept any number from a particular community

indicators.note: to accept means the jumbled letters take in the number
badly signals the letters are jumbled

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An English person itches badly to accept anyone from a particular community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' turns ITCH into THIC; 'to accept' then puts N inside, giving THNIC after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a group sharing common national or cultural origins.

clue.text: One retiring will consume small dish

indicators.note: will consume means the timid person swallows the letter inside

parts.note: a shy, retiring person is called a mouse

explanation.surface: A shy person will eat a small dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert or savoury preparation served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Odds on second one mentioned to make a splash

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds offered on a horse at the start of a race
the latter is the second of two things just named

explanation.surface: A betting tip about the second runner mentioned, hoping to make a big impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a splash' looks figurative (cause a stir) but is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash is to scatter liquid about in drops, which is what the verb describes.

clue.text: The point of frosty weather?

parts.note: seemingly asks the purpose of cold weather, but describes a pointed spike of frozen water

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles: what is the point of frosty weather?
explanation.definitionFit: A tapering spike of ice hanging from eaves is literally a point produced by freezing conditions.

clue.text: Summarise London area studies first

indicators.note: first places the studies before the London region

parts.note: two synonyms for studies: to con is to study, and a den is a study or private room
SE is South East, the region of England around London

explanation.surface: To summarise a London area, study it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Studies' gives two words, CON (verb) and DEN (noun), side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to shorten a text while keeping its essential content.

clue.text: One might cut commercials when broadcast

indicators.note: when broadcast means the word is spoken out, so we go by its sound

parts.note: ads are commercials, advertisements

explanation.surface: A TV channel might cut its commercials when broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle, used for shaping wood.

clue.text: Place of worship a celebrant organised

indicators.note: organised means the letters are arranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A priest arranges matters at a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent sanctuary of the Israelites, or a nonconformist chapel: both sacred buildings.
